chunks.arabic_text: ٢٨ - عَلِيّ بْن أَحْمَد بْن نَصْرٍ، الْبَنْدَنِيجِيّ، أَبُو الْحَسَنِ، سَكَنَ الرَّمْلَة.

translations.en: 28 – Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nasr, al-Bandaniji, Abu al-Hasan. He settled in al-Ramla.
Weak, collapsed, he is not turned to.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Bandaniji, a resident of Ramla, as a weak narrator (*da'if*) whose transmission style is described as *mutahaf*, implying a lack of precision or structural integrity in his narrations. In Shia hadith criticism, such detailed characterization helps scholars distinguish between minor weaknesses and those severe enough to exclude a narrator from reliable chains (*isnad*), ensuring the authenticity of transmitted teachings.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaniji and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (in terms of reliability or precision in narration)
key_terms.مُتَهَافِتٌ: Collapsed/Disjointed (referring to the quality of transmission, often implying haste or lack of precision)
key_terms.الرَّمْلَة: Ramla (a city in Palestine, indicating the narrator's place of residence)
